q: A die is thrown once. What is the probability of getting an odd number?
exp: Odd outcomes are 1, 3 and 5, so probability = 3/6 = 1/2.

q: A die is thrown once. What is the probability of getting a number less than 3?
exp: The favorable outcomes are 1 and 2. Probability = 2/6 = 1/3.

q: A die is thrown once. What is the probability of getting a multiple of 3?
exp: Multiples of 3 are 3 and 6. Probability = 2/6 = 1/3.

q: A die is thrown once. What is the probability of getting a number greater than 2 and less than 6?
exp: Favorable outcomes are 3, 4 and 5. Probability = 3/6 = 1/2.

q: Two dice are thrown together. What is the probability that the sum is 8?
exp: The favorable outcomes are (2,6),(3,5),(4,4),(5,3),(6,2), giving 5/36.

q: Two dice are thrown together. What is the probability that the sum is less than 5?
exp: Sums 2, 3 and 4 have 1+2+3 = 6 outcomes. Probability = 6/36 = 1/6.

q: Two dice are thrown together. What is the probability that the sum is greater than 9?
exp: Sums greater than 9 are 10, 11 and 12, with 3+2+1 = 6 outcomes. Probability = 6/36 = 1/6.

q: Two dice are thrown together. What is the probability of getting at least one 6?
exp: Probability of no 6 = (5/6)^2 = 25/36. Therefore, probability of at least one 6 = 11/36.

q: Two dice are thrown together. What is the probability that both numbers are even?
exp: Each die has 3 even faces. Probability = 3/6 × 3/6 = 1/4.

q: Two dice are thrown together. What is the probability that the product is even?
exp: The product is odd only when both dice are odd: probability = 1/4. Hence product even = 1−1/4 = 3/4.

q: A coin is tossed twice. What is the probability of getting exactly one head?
exp: The favorable outcomes are HT and TH. Probability = 2/4 = 1/2.

q: A coin is tossed three times. What is the probability of getting at least one tail?
exp: The only outcome without a tail is HHH, with probability 1/8. Therefore, probability = 1−1/8 = 7/8.

q: A coin is tossed three times. What is the probability of getting at most one head?
exp: At most one head means 0 or 1 head. Outcomes: TTT, HTT, THT, TTH = 4 out of 8. Probability = 1/2.

q: A coin is tossed three times. What is the probability of getting at least two heads?
exp: Exactly two heads has 3 outcomes and exactly three heads has 1 outcome. Probability = 4/8 = 1/2.

q: Four coins are tossed together. What is the probability of getting exactly two heads?
exp: There are 4C2 = 6 favorable outcomes out of 2^4 = 16. Probability = 6/16 = 3/8.

q: A card is drawn from a standard deck of 52 cards. What is the probability of getting a queen?
exp: There are 4 queens in 52 cards. Probability = 4/52 = 1/13.

q: A card is drawn from a standard deck. What is the probability of getting a black card?
exp: There are 26 black cards in a 52-card deck. Probability = 26/52 = 1/2.

q: A card is drawn from a standard deck. What is the probability of getting a red ace?
exp: There are two red aces, hearts and diamonds. Probability = 2/52 = 1/26.

q: A card is drawn from a standard deck. What is the probability of getting a card that is neither an ace nor a king?
exp: There are 4 aces and 4 kings, so 44 cards are neither. Probability = 44/52 = 11/13.

q: A card is drawn from a standard deck. What is the probability of getting a jack, queen or king?
exp: There are 12 such face cards. Probability = 12/52 = 3/13.

q: A card is drawn from a standard deck. What is the probability of getting a spade or a heart?
exp: Spades and hearts contain 13 cards each, giving 26 favorable cards. Probability = 26/52 = 1/2.

q: A card is drawn from a standard deck. What is the probability of getting a red face card?
exp: There are 6 red face cards: 3 hearts and 3 diamonds. Probability = 6/52 = 3/26.

q: A card is drawn from a standard deck. What is the probability of getting an ace or a king?
exp: There are 4 aces and 4 kings, with no overlap. Probability = 8/52 = 2/13.

q: A bag contains 6 red balls and 4 blue balls. One ball is drawn. What is the probability of getting a red ball?
exp: There are 6 red balls out of 10 total. Probability = 6/10 = 3/5.

q: A bag contains 5 white and 7 black balls. One ball is drawn. What is the probability of getting a black ball?
exp: There are 7 black balls out of 12 total. Probability = 7/12.

q: A bag contains 3 red and 2 green balls. Two balls are drawn without replacement. What is the probability of getting at least one red ball?
exp: Probability of no red = both green = 2/5×1/4 = 1/10. Hence at least one red = 1−1/10 = 9/10.

q: A bag contains 5 red, 4 blue and 3 green balls. One ball is drawn. What is the probability of getting neither red nor blue?
exp: Only the 3 green balls satisfy the condition. Probability = 3/12 = 1/4.

q: A die is thrown once. What is the probability of getting a number that is not prime?
exp: Non-prime outcomes are 1, 4 and 6. Probability = 3/6 = 1/2.

q: A die is thrown once. What is the probability of getting neither an even number nor a multiple of 3?
exp: Numbers that are neither even nor multiples of 3 are only 1 and 5. Probability = 2/6 = 1/3.

q: Two dice are thrown together. What is the probability that the sum is 4 or 10?
exp: Sum 4 has 3 outcomes and sum 10 has 3 outcomes. Total = 6/36 = 1/6.

q: Two dice are thrown together. What is the probability that the sum is either 2 or 12?
exp: Sum 2 occurs as (1,1) and sum 12 as (6,6). There are 2 favorable outcomes out of 36. Probability = 1/18.

q: Three coins are tossed. What is the probability of getting at least one head and at least one tail?
exp: Exclude HHH and TTT from the 8 outcomes. Six outcomes remain, so probability = 6/8 = 3/4.

q: Three coins are tossed. What is the probability of getting exactly one tail?
exp: There are 3 outcomes with exactly one tail: THH, HTH and HHT. Probability = 3/8.

q: A card is drawn from a standard deck. What is the probability of getting a card that is neither red nor an ace?
exp: There are 26 black cards, of which 2 are aces. Thus 24 cards are black and non-aces. Probability = 24/52 = 6/13.

q: Two cards are drawn from a standard deck without replacement. What is the probability that both are red?
exp: There are 26 red cards. Probability = 26/52×25/51 = 25/102.

exp: Probability of no 5 = 5/6×5/6 = 25/36. Therefore, at least one 5 = 11/36.

q: A die is thrown twice. What is the probability of getting exactly one 6?
exp: Exactly one 6 can occur in two ways: 6 followed by non-6 or non-6 followed by 6. Probability = 2×1/6×5/6 = 5/18.

q: A die is thrown twice. What is the probability that neither throw gives a 6?
exp: Each throw has probability 5/6 of not being 6. Therefore, probability = (5/6)^2 = 25/36.

q: A bag contains 8 red and 2 blue balls. Two balls are drawn without replacement. What is the probability that at least one is blue?
exp: Probability of no blue = 8/10×7/9 = 28/45. Hence at least one blue = 1−28/45 = 17/45.

q: A bag contains 6 red and 4 blue balls. Two balls are drawn without replacement. What is the probability of getting at most one red ball?
exp: At most one red means either both blue or one red and one blue. P(both blue)=4/10×3/9=2/15. P(one each)=6/10×4/9×2=8/15. Total = 10/15 = 2/3.

q: If P(A)=1/3 and P(B)=1/4 and A and B are mutually exclusive, what is P(A or B)?
exp: For mutually exclusive events, P(A or B)=P(A)+P(B)=1/3+1/4=7/12.

q: If the probability of an event is 3/5, what is the probability that the event does not occur?
exp: Complementary probability = 1−3/5 = 2/5.

q: A box contains 5 red, 3 blue and 2 green balls. What is the probability of drawing a ball that is not green?
exp: There are 8 non-green balls out of 10. Probability = 8/10 = 4/5.

q: A card is drawn from a standard deck. What is the probability that it is either a spade or an ace?
exp: There are 13 spades and 4 aces, but the ace of spades is counted twice. Favorable cards = 13+4−1 = 16. Probability = 16/52 = 4/13.
